subject: Request: SAML session timeline and SCIM sync logs for SOC2 audit
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@carebridge.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: security@carebridge.com
Date: Sat, 7 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SOC 2 evidence request — session and provisioning artifacts

Hi Jordan,

We're in the middle of our SOC 2 readiness window and the auditor asked for two items related to your SSO/SCIM setup: a timeline of recent SAML sessions for a sample user (covering Oct 20–Nov 5) showing assertion timestamps and IPs, and a sampling of SCIM sync logs that show provisioning/updates for service accounts and role changes.

Can you point me to the files or drop a couple of redacted samples? We just need enough to validate assertion timestamps align with access grants and to confirm SCIM delta behavior around role updates. If you have a short note on how you retain/rotate assertion logs (retention period, redaction policy) that would help too.

Thanks — we need this by COB Nov 10 to keep the audit timeline.

—Maya
Security & Compliance, CareBridge
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@carebridge.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com, security@carebridge.com
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SOC 2 evidence request — session and provisioning artifacts

Maya — thanks for the clear ask. Short answer: yes, we can provide redacted SAML assertion timelines and a SCIM sync snapshot. High level plan below and I'll attach samples in a follow-up: 

- Provide redacted SAML assertion timeline for requested window (we'll mask full usernames and only surface assertion ID, timestamp, relying party, IP, and outcome).
- Export SCIM delta logs for the period containing role changes and service-account provisioning events; we'll redact PII and include a short mapping to our role IDs.
- Include a short retention note: assertion logs kept 90 days by default, with a 365-day longer-retention tier for Dedicated customers; redaction policy documented.

Irene (cc) — can you pull the SCIM delta CSV and session timeline snippet from the logs for Oct 20–Nov 5 and attach a role ownership matrix? I can scrub and upload to the shared Drive link.

I'll aim to have the samples and the short retention statement by tomorrow afternoon (Nov 10 COB PST). If the auditor needs different fields, call it out and we'll adjust.

-Jordan
Senior Technical Account Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@carebridge.com>, security@carebridge.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 08:33:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SOC 2 evidence request — session and provisioning artifacts

Jordan / Maya — pulling the exports now. A couple clarifying asks so we provide the exact columns the auditor expects: 

1) For SAML timeline sample — do they want the full assertion XML for any sessions, or is the assertion metadata (assertion_id, authn_instant, subject (redacted), issuer, audience, src_ip, result) sufficient?
2) For SCIM — we'll export core delta events with event_type (create/update/delete), timestamp, user_external_id (redacted), scim_patch payload (redacted), target_role_id. Would a mapping table of target_role_id -> human role name be helpful (we can attach an xlsx)?

I can produce: saml-session-timeline-sample.txt, scim-sync-log-snapshot.csv, and role-ownership-matrix.xlsx. We will redact emails/usernames and replace with stable internal ids (e.g., user_8245) for auditor traceability.

If CareBridge security prefers we also include a short readme describing redaction steps and retention windows, we can add that as well.

—Irene
Sr. Compliance Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@carebridge.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, security@carebridge.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 13:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SOC 2 evidence request — session and provisioning artifacts

Maya — attaching the redacted samples (see attachments). Brief notes included inline: 

Attachment: saml-session-timeline-sample.txt (snippet) — columns: assertion_id, authn_instant, issuer, audience, src_ip, ttl_seconds, outcome. User identifiers replaced with user_[id].
Attachment: scim-sync-log-snapshot.csv — delta events (create/update), timestamp, event_type, user_external_id (redacted), target_role_id, change_summary.
Attachment: role-ownership-matrix.xlsx — maps target_role_id -> role_name -> owner_email.

Retention & redaction summary (short): assertion XMLs retained 90 days by default; for Dedicated customers we keep 365 days. PII is redacted in artifacts provided to third parties; redaction replaces email/username with stable ids and strips raw IPs in any public-facing document (auditor copies will include full src_ip when NDAs are in place).

If the auditor wants raw assertion XMLs with full headers (they usually request that under NDA), let us know and we can escalate to Legal for an NDA and a temporary, encrypted transfer.

-Jordan

Attachments referenced: saml-session-timeline-sample.txt (included), scim-sync-log-snapshot.csv (included), role-ownership-matrix.xlsx (included)
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@carebridge.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SOC 2 evidence request — session and provisioning artifacts

Maya — confirm receipt of the three artifacts from Jordan/Irene. A few quick operational notes from our side to make the auditor review go smoother: 

- The session timeline file was sampled to remove high-volume noise; it contains 25 assertions across the requested window for one representative user_id. If the auditor asks for additional samples, we can produce up to 100 assertions per request.
- The SCIM snapshot contains delta events for service accounts and role changes; we included the change_summary column to show what changed (e.g., added role_id 204 -> role_name: data_readonly).
- If the auditor wants IP addresses preserved for chain-of-custody validation we can exchange the files over our secure SFTP (we'll request an NDA from CareBridge).

Next steps: if you confirm the auditor has what they need, we'll mark this delivered in HubSpot CB-000451 and close out the ticket. If they ask for raw assertion XMLs we will initiate the NDA route and coordinate a secure drop.

Sean Gallagher
Compliance Operations Lead, Redwood Inference
--- End of thread ---
